title: High Temperature Fan Heat Path
description: Two illustrative side views of high temperature fans with ten labeled parts. For each part the learner commits a job (Block, Shed or Allow) before its description is revealed, in any order, one attempt each, with mastery at 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt. After the quiz the drawing can be filtered by job and every description reread in Explore mode.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: How high temperature fan parts block heat, shed heat or allow thermal growth
learningObjectives: The learner will classify ten high temperature fan parts by whether each one blocks heat, sheds heat, or allows thermal growth, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.

accessibility.notes: Every part is a focusable role=button (Tab walks them in label order 1-10, then Enter or Space); keys 1-3 choose Block, Shed or Allow; after an answer focus moves to Next part. Verdicts and prompts are announced through FP.announce (aria-live), and the incorrect verdict names the right job. ✓/✗ glyphs, part badges and solid/dashed label borders pair with colour. Below 560 px the labels shrink to their part numbers in a larger font; the prompt and infobox name the part.

controls.label: 1. Block / 2. Shed / 3. Allow
controls.purpose: Commit the job of the highlighted part (keys 1-3)

controls.purpose: Go to the next unanswered part (Enter)

rules: Each of the 10 parts takes one answer (Block, Shed or Allow); correctness is an exact match with the spec's Job column.
Parts may be answered in any order; an answered part cannot be re-answered.
The description is shown only after the answer is committed.
Score: n of 10 correct; mastery is 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
Part 10 (fixed bearing) is scored Allow because fixing one end sends all growth toward the floating bearing.
assumptions: One generic belt-driven fan drawing combines features FanPedia shows on different pedestal forms (high temp angle, separated pedestal gap, motor heat shield) so that all eight parts appear together.
limitations: Illustrative drawings, not to scale and not a specific Twin City Fan model.
The quiz opens with the shaft cooler selected; any other part can be selected instead.

sources: FanPedia: The Fan & Blower Encyclopedia, pp. 85, 90, 110-113 and 192

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict then reveal: the learner classifies each part's job before its description is shown, then filters the drawing by job
keyQuestions: Does this part block heat, shed heat, or allow growth?
Why is a cooler box left uninsulated?
Why does a hot fan need one fixed and one floating bearing?
Which parts deal with the shaft heat path, and which with the pedestal?
commonMisconceptions: A cooler box is an insulated enclosure (it is deliberately left uninsulated so the cooler can shed heat).
Insulation pins are themselves insulation (they hold the insulation that blocks heat).
Every high temperature part is about keeping heat out (the floating bearing instead lets the shaft grow).
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score shown as 'First-attempt score: n of 10'; mastery is 8 of 10 on the first attempt.
